s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with palpitations and transient loss of consciousness
salient_findings: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode
Diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and mid-right coronary artery
key_facts: Reported palpitation and amaurosis before loss of consciousness
Previous episode of syncope 1 month prior
Vital signs: blood pressure 125/96 mm Hg, pulse rate 81 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 99% under ambient air
Normal laboratory tests, including blood glucose, electrolytes, D-dimer, troponin I, and N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide
Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring
50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD
Minimum lumen area of 5.92 mm2 in proximal LAD, with plaque burden of 74%

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: QTc of 403 milliseconds and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring and previous episode of syncope

shortlist.label: Coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: 50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and 80% stenosis in mid-right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Palpitation and amaurosis before loss of consciousness, and left ventricular ejection fraction of 58%

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia recorded during 24-hour Holter monitoring and recurrent syncope

raw.rationale: The patient experienced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during a presyncope episode, which is a hallmark of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. The normal electrocardiogram and echocardiography results, along with the presence of ventricular tachycardia during Holter monitoring, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The QTc interval of 403 milliseconds is within the normal range, making Long QT syndrome less likely.

rejected.label: Coronary artery disease
rejected.why: While the patient has significant coronary artery stenosis, the symptoms of syncope and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia are not typical of coronary artery disease alone.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of left ventricular hypertrophy on echocardiography, making this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The echocardiography results did not show any evidence of right ventricular dysfunction or fibrofatty replacement, which is characteristic of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.

gold: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) with Giant R-wave Syndrome
